title: De'Mond Parker's 291 Yards Against Texas in 1997
question: Who holds the record for most rushing yards in an Oklahoma-Texas game?
answer: Oklahoma's De'Mond Parker ran for 291 yards against Texas on Oct. 11, 1997, the most by any player in the Red River rivalry. The Sooners still lost 27-24.
summary: De'Mond Parker rushed for 291 yards in Oklahoma's 27-24 loss to Texas in 1997, the top mark in the Red River rivalry and third on OU's single-game list.
body: Oklahoma fans remember plenty of Red River games for the final score. The 1997 meeting at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas is remembered for one runner who did everything except get the win. Sophomore tailback De'Mond Parker carried 31 times for 291 yards, a figure that still stands as the most any player has gained in the history of the Oklahoma-Texas series.

Parker averaged better than nine yards a carry, and his day included long scoring runs of 48 and 66 yards by one account and 44 and 66 by another, so the details of his touchdowns vary from source to source. What the record books agree on is the total. His 291 yards rank third on Oklahoma's all-time single-game rushing list, behind only Samaje Perine's 427 against Kansas in 2014 and Greg Pruitt's 294 against Kansas State in 1971.

He also did it against a Heisman-bound opponent. Texas running back Ricky Williams carried 40 times for 223 yards, and the two backs spent the afternoon trading big gains. In the end the difference was a kicker. Texas's Phil Dawson booted a 51-yard field goal with just under five minutes left, and the Longhorns escaped with a 27-24 win in front of a crowd of 75,587.

Parker went on to finish his Sooner career in 1998 with more than 1,000 rushing yards in each of his three seasons, and he sits among the program's top ten career rushers. For one October afternoon in Dallas, though, he put together the best individual performance either school has ever seen in this rivalry.
